thread:
maya: Heads up — after last night's resharding I'm seeing weird p95 jumps on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate. No deploys. p50 steady, p95 moves ~80ms on some clients. Anyone else?
callum: same, noticed at ~03:20 UTC. Only affected a subset of endpoints behind the US-e exitnode.
linh: can you paste the route + variant? sounds like a sampling/provenance mismatch to me :thinking:
maya: route=/v1/generate; model=rwkv-2-small; variant=quantized-v2.
deploy-bot: "deploy-bot: Reshard operation completed by infra at 2024-02-23T02:45:00Z (change-id: rs-20240223-7). No model restarts."
sam: if resharding moved some clients to different pools the sample origin labels might flip between gateway-sampled vs agent-sampled. percentiles can shift a lot when sample pools change.
anika: agreed. we saw similar when we moved mobile clients to the new edge pool last quarter; small p95 shifts but looked larger because the sample source changed.
callum: quick sanity check — can someone run a query for sample_origin on that time window? e.g.:
```
select sample_origin, percentile(95, latency_ms) from latency where route='/v1/generate' and ts between '2024-02-23T02:30:00Z' and '2024-02-23T03:30:00Z' group by sample_origin;
```
linh: running now. giving results: gateway: p95=220ms (count 12000), agent: p95=140ms (count 4800). total p95 computed on merged samples becomes ~200ms.
maya: aha — so the merged p95 increased because the gateway-origin samples have heavier tail. But why did gateway samples spike post-reshard?
sam: hypothesis: reshard moved a subset of clients that hit the KV cache cold (misses) in frontends that still tag origin as gateway. more KV misses => extra compute => longer tail.
anika: also check routing weights. if some traffic got redirected to a slower variant temporarily that would inflate gateway sample p95. callum, can you check rollout logs?
callum: looked — there was a brief canary bump for a different model variant (not rwkv) around 02:40, unrelated. No explicit routing weight change for this route.
linh: digging into kvcache hit rates by host: host-12 had hit-rate drop from 92% -> 58% starting 02:46. correlated with gateway-origin p95 increase.
maya: so root cause looks like reshard caused some requests to land on nodes with cold kvcache. gateway sampling included those requests; agent sampling (post-attach) didn't include them as much, so merged p95 jumped.
sam: long-term fix: we should annotate dashboard percentiles with sample_origin breakdown (gateway/agent/cache-hit/cache-miss) and expose a small toggle to compute p95 only for a chosen provenance. UX: add provenance pill beside percentile.
anika: agree — also add a tooltip explaining merge semantics: when UI shows global p95 it's computed on merged samples which can be dominated by origin-specific tails.
callum: short-term: add an alert rule to detect >30% delta between global p95 and p95(agent) or p95(gateway) for a route. That would catch provenance-driven jumps.
linh: +1. I'll add a query panel and a probe to telemetry. proposed alert query:
```
abs(percentile(95, merged) - max(percentile(95, gateway), percentile(95, agent))) > 30
```
maya: also can we surface sample counts next to pctl values? low counts should reduce confidence.
anika: yes — show count + 95% conf interval or just a tiny warning icon if sample_count < 1k in window.
callum: ops question — do quota/fallbacks affect sample provenance? if we throttle at the gateway and fallback to a smaller model, merged p95 could change.
sam: quotas will. fallback weight changes are in routing policies and they should set a distinct sample tag. we need to ensure policy-driven fallbacks set sample_origin=fallback to avoid hiding the source.
maya: action items: 1) Linh to add provenance panel + sample counts to the pctl widget (PR). 2) Callum to add alert on pctl divergence. 3) Anika to update docs/tooltip text for merge semantics. 4) Sam to verify routing policy tags set sample_origin for fallbacks.
linh: started a branch for the panel, will ping for review.
callum: I'll own the alert and add playbook note.
maya: thanks. one final ask — can we backfill sample_origin for last 48h so we can run a retrospective? that'll help confirm KV cache correlation.
linh: backfill queued, ETA ~45m. will post results.
deploy-bot: "deploy-bot: Telemetry backfill job started (job-id: tb-20240223-91)."
maya: great — mark this resolved after backfill confirms correlation and we land small UI changes. :+1:
callum: noted, moving to follow-up board.
